newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fiat says world car doing well.
newsitem.headline: Fiat says world car doing well.

text.p: Fiat Auto deputy administrator Roberto Testore said the performance of the company's so-called world car, the Palio built in Brazil, had exceeded expectations and he expected 150,000 orders before the end of the year.

"The car's success exceeds the expectations we had," Testore told reporters at the Paris car show. The Palio is the first of a five-car family being built on the same platform and will be followed by a stationwagon, pickup and other versions.
Testore said the group was pleased with the success of the Bravo/Brava lower mid-sized car, which represented 70 percent of Fiat sales increases in France this year.
He said Fiat expected to end the year with around eight percent of the French market up from 6.4 percent in 1995.

He estimated the French market at around two million cars next year if some assistance measures are adopted after the expiry at the start of this week of a year-long state new-cars-for-old rebate scheme.

Testore said he thought the French government would adopt new measures -- "not right away, and slightly different from the rebate scheme, and with some new aid, we could have a market of around two million, slightly under 1996 but not much."

Fiat has been hurt by sluggish spending in Italy and Testore said third-quarter car sales in Italy had not been encouraging, but he said its sales in Europe outside Italy were expected to end the year 40 percent higher.
Among the company's exhibits at the show was a much-admired Alfa Romeo concept car, the Nuvola, described by Testore as "a concept car with ambitions".
